bio.topic: Limiting factors of photosynthesis and investigations

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the term for the factor that is in shortest supply and therefore restricts the rate of photosynthesis.
questions.hint: It 'limits' the rate.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which of these is NOT usually a limiting factor of photosynthesis?
questions.hint: Think about which substances are reactants or affect enzymes.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a pondweed experiment, what is usually counted to measure the rate of photosynthesis?
questions.hint: Which product is a gas?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A lamp is moved closer to a pondweed. What is the independent variable?
questions.hint: The independent variable is the one you change.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why is a beaker of water often placed between the lamp and the pondweed?
options: To absorb heat so temperature stays constant
questions.answer: To absorb heat so temperature stays constant
questions.hint: Lamps give out more than light.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Sodium hydrogencarbonate is added to the water around pondweed. What does it provide?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: On a graph of rate against light intensity, the line rises and then levels off. What does the levelling off show?
questions.hint: Adding more light no longer increases the rate.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Above about 40 °C, the rate of photosynthesis falls sharply. Why?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the colour of hydrogencarbonate indicator in air with normal (atmospheric) carbon dioxide concentration?
questions.hint: It is between the high-CO₂ and low-CO₂ colours.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Hydrogencarbonate indicator turns purple. What does this show about the carbon dioxide concentration?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A leaf is sealed in a tube of hydrogencarbonate indicator and kept in the dark. What colour will the indicator turn?
questions.hint: In the dark the leaf can respire but cannot photosynthesise.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A tube with indicator but no leaf is set up alongside the others. What is its purpose?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A pondweed produced 36 bubbles in 3 minutes. Calculate the rate of photosynthesis in bubbles per minute.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Light intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the lamp. If the distance is doubled, the light intensity becomes…
questions.hint: Use 1/d².

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why do some greenhouse growers burn paraffin heaters in winter?
options: To increase both temperature and carbon dioxide
questions.answer: To increase both temperature and carbon dioxide
questions.hint: Think about the products of combustion.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why counting bubbles is a less accurate method than collecting the gas in a measuring cylinder or gas syringe, and suggest one other way to improve the reliability of the investigation.
questions.hint: Think about bubble size and repeats.

bss.topic: Abertura política, Anistia e Diretas Já

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como ficou conhecido o projeto do governo militar, iniciado em 1974, de devolver o poder aos civis aos poucos?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano foi aprovada a Lei da Anistia no Brasil?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual era o slogan dos movimentos que pediam uma anistia sem restrições? Anistia ampla, geral e ___.
questions.hint: Significa 'sem restrições'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual Ato Institucional, considerado o mais duro da ditadura, deixou de valer no início de 1979?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem foram beneficiados pela Lei da Anistia de 1979?
options: Opositores e também agentes do Estado acusados de crimes
questions.answer: Opositores e também agentes do Estado acusados de crimes
questions.hint: A lei foi chamada de 'recíproca'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual foi uma consequência direta da anistia de 1979?
options: O retorno de exilados ao Brasil
O fim imediato do governo militar
questions.answer: O retorno de exilados ao Brasil

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em 1979, a reforma partidária acabou com qual sistema?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em 1982, os brasileiros voltaram a votar diretamente para qual cargo?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual movimento popular de 1983–1984 pedia eleições diretas para presidente?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que propunha a emenda constitucional defendida pelo movimento Diretas Já?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que aconteceu com essa emenda na votação de abril de 1984?
options: Foi rejeitada por não alcançar votos suficientes
questions.answer: Foi rejeitada por não alcançar votos suficientes
questions.hint: Ela precisava de dois terços da Câmara.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como foi escolhido o primeiro presidente civil, em 1985?
options: Pelo Colégio Eleitoral, de forma indireta
questions.answer: Pelo Colégio Eleitoral, de forma indireta

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual palavra designa o processo de volta à democracia no Brasil nos anos 1980?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual documento, promulgado em 1988, marcou juridicamente o fim da transição?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que a abertura política foi chamada de 'lenta e gradual' e por que os militares preferiram controlar o ritmo da transição.
questions.hint: Pense em quem queria evitar mudanças bruscas e por quê.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Analise por que a Lei da Anistia de 1979 é até hoje debatida no Brasil, considerando quem foi beneficiado por ela.
questions.hint: Compare a anistia pedida pelos movimentos com a lei aprovada.

bus.topic: Financial and non-financial methods of motivation

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A worker is paid £12 for every hour worked. This is an example of…

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A fixed annual amount paid in equal monthly instalments is called…

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the term for payment based on a percentage of the value of sales made?
questions.hint: Common for sales staff.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is a financial method of motivation?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a non-financial method of motivation?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What term describes workers moving between different tasks at the same skill level?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Giving workers more tasks of a similar level of difficulty is called…
questions.hint: Think of 'larger' job, not 'richer'.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Giving workers more challenging tasks and responsibility is called…

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A salesperson earns a basic salary of $1,500 a month plus 5% commission. In one month she sells $20,000 of goods. Calculate her total pay in dollars.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A worker earns £14 per hour and works 38 hours a week. Calculate the weekly wage in pounds.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: One disadvantage of commission for a business is that…
options: staff may pressure customers into buying
it is hard to calculate pay
it removes the incentive to sell
questions.answer: staff may pressure customers into buying

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which method is most likely to suit a production line worker doing repetitive tasks?
questions.hint: Which reduces boredom?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Organising workers into groups responsible for a whole section of work is called…

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A disadvantage of job rotation for a business is that…

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of paying a bonus to factory workers.
questions.hint: Think about output and quality.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A clothing shop wants to motivate its sales assistants. Evaluate whether commission or job enrichment would be the better method. Justify your answer.
questions.hint: Consider cost, behaviour with customers and long-term motivation.

chem.topic: Electrolysis of molten compounds and aqueous solutions

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is electrolysis?
options: The breakdown of an ionic compound using electricity
The dissolving of a salt in water
The reaction of an acid with a base
questions.answer: The breakdown of an ionic compound using electricity

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What name is given to the liquid or solution that conducts electricity and is broken down in electrolysis?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which electrode is negative?
questions.hint: Positive ions move towards it.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why must an ionic compound be molten or dissolved to be electrolysed?
options: So the ions are free to move
So electrons can move through the solid
questions.answer: So the ions are free to move

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why are graphite or platinum used as electrodes?
options: They are inert and conduct electricity
questions.answer: They are inert and conduct electricity

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Molten lead(II) bromide is electrolysed. What forms at the cathode?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Molten lead(II) bromide is electrolysed. What is seen at the anode?
questions.hint: Think about what bromine looks like.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which half-equation shows the reaction at the cathode for molten sodium chloride?
questions.hint: Reduction is gain of electrons.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In aqueous solutions, hydrogen is produced at the cathode if the metal is…

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride (brine) is electrolysed. What forms at the anode?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Brine is electrolysed with inert electrodes. What forms at the cathode?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Name the solution left behind after the electrolysis of brine.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Aqueous copper(II) sulfate is electrolysed with graphite electrodes. What forms at the cathode?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Aqueous copper(II) sulfate is electrolysed with graphite electrodes. What forms at the anode?
questions.hint: Sulfate ions are not discharged.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: During electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate with graphite electrodes, the blue colour of the solution…
questions.hint: Copper ions are being removed.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Copper(II) sulfate solution is electrolysed using copper electrodes. Describe and explain what happens to the mass of each electrode.
questions.hint: Think about which electrode loses copper ions and which gains copper atoms.
